subject: Order form indemnity: evidence expectations and carveout alignment
messages:
From: Amelia Jones <amelia.jones@orchidai.com>

Cc: procurement@orchidai.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Draft order form — indemnity scope questions

Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft order form this morning. We reviewed the indemnity section and have a few open items we want to align on before we route back to legal:

- Third-party claims: we want a clear definition of when Orchid would route a claim to Redwood and what the evidence package must include.
- AI-generated output: our counsel is asking whether the standard IP indemnity covers claims arising from model outputs (e.g., hallucinated infringement allegations). Can you confirm Redwood's position?
- Open-source / downstream dependencies: can we confirm there are no additional liabilities for OSS used in Redwood's stack (we requested a list in procurement but haven't received it).

I've attached our redline for the order form (Orchid_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx). Would you and your legal team be available for a short call tomorrow to walk through the compromises?

If it helps, procurement will join and we can put the draft language in DocuSign once we have legal alignment.

Best,
Amelia Jones
Head of Procurement, Orchid AI
[Attachment: Orchid_OrderForm_Redline_v1.docx (docx, 72 KB)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Jones <amelia.jones@orchidai.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form — indemnity scope questions

Amelia — thanks for the redline and the clear bullets. Internal legal (Kimberly) and I discussed. Summary proposal below so we can go into the call with a concise starting point:

- Third-party claims: we agree on a notice-and-cooperation flow. Customer (Orchid) must provide a written notice within 30 days of becoming aware, and an evidence packet (claims, alleged materials, sample outputs). Redwood to have right to assume defense for claims that directly allege Redwood's breach of the agreement or Redwood-provided model code.

- AI-generated output: Redwood is comfortable offering indemnity only when the claim arises from (i) a willful infringement in model weights/code we supplied, or (ii) use of a customer-provided fine-tuned model that Redwood modified negligently. We cannot accept open-ended indemnity for all hallucination-style allegations — propose carveout language.

- Open-source dependencies: Redwood will list third-party OSS components used in the supported runtime upon request and agrees not to indemnify for OSS license claims beyond our express modifications.

- Financial cap: propose a per-claim cap equal to the annual fees paid under the order form, with mutual obligations to mitigate.

Kimberly, can you draft two short redline options (defend-vs-reimburse and limited defend-only) that we can present on the call? Ben — wanted you in the loop on the evidence requirements (ops will need to be able to pull logs).

Propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow 10:30am ET.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Rdw-Proposed-Indemnity-Notes.pdf (pdf, 18 KB)]

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft order form — indemnity scope questions

Marissa / Ben — quick legal notes and two suggested snippets for the order form. I kept them short so commercial can pick.

1) Notice & evidence: require written notice within 30 days, plus a minimum evidence set (initial claim notice, exemplar outputs alleged to infringe, relevant customer data slice, and a statement of the legal theory). We will add a 14-day SLA for the customer to produce missing evidence once requested.

2) Defense control: prefer Redwood to assume defense where the claim is based on alleged infringement of Redwood-owned model code or model weights delivered by Redwood. For model output allegations (hallucinations), offer: 

   Option A (Defend-vs-Reimburse): "Redwood will defend and indemnify Customer for third-party claims alleging infringement of third-party intellectual property resulting from Redwood's Model as delivered; where the claim arises primarily from Customer's prompts or customer-supplied data, Customer shall reimburse Redwood for reasonable defense costs."

   Option B (Limited Defend Only): "Redwood will indemnify Customer for third-party claims to the extent directly attributable to material defects in Redwood-supplied Model code or weights; Redwood's indemnity does not extend to claims arising solely from model outputs unconnected to such defects (including hallucinations)."

3) OSS carveout: include explicit carveout for widely-used OSS license claims unless the claim relates to Redwood's proprietary modifications. Also provide a schedule (separate doc) where Redwood names high-level OSS components (no detailed SBOM in contract).

4) Evidence & cooperation: require customer to preserve evidence and allow Redwood to access runtime logs under an NDA and reasonable notice—ops needs at least 48 hours to collect live logs.

If commercial wants to be aggressive on cap amounts, note we can trade a higher cap for additional warranties or an insurance endorsement.

Kimberly Park
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Amelia Jones <amelia.jones@orchidai.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai, procurement@orchidai.com
Date: Tue, 12 May 2026 08:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Draft order form — indemnity scope questions

Amelia — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached are two short redline options and a mutual action plan so procurement can track next steps. High-level compromise we are prepared to present:

- Redwood offers indemnity for third-party IP claims tied to Redwood-supplied code/weights and for a narrow set of model-output claims that can be traced to such defects.
- Claims driven solely by customer prompts, customer-provided training data, or hallucinations are outside Redwood's indemnity scope; Redwood will cooperate and provide logs under NDA.
- Per-claim cap: annual fees (commercial can consider an insurance endorsement in lieu of a higher cap).
- Evidence package: initial claim notice + exemplar outputs + sample customer data + claim theory; 14-day cure/evidence window; 48-hour ops log collection notice.

Proposed next step: 30-minute call today 10:30am ET to walk through the two redline options and confirm which path Orchid prefers. If we align, procurement can start the signature workflow.

Thanks,
Marissa
